title: Python attribute-write read-side: F1 restricted bypass, F2 any-base gated mark, F3 reads, and the written-base counterexample (DEC-303 a89 fallback)
description: Ordinary follow-up carved out of opum-ai/glyph-cli#242 by the DEC-303 (a89) item 2 fallback (ODOC-640, opum-ai/opum-doc#2098, opum-doc agreed). #242 round 1 APPROVED its head 034a898a, which landed as opum-ai/glyph-cli#243 at dev fee6946a; round 2 then BLOCKED on a finding F1's fix introduced, so the fix commit 3b1ace313dedce1c21eea0639cccfc2ce24b9677 was dropped and is kept reachable on branch fix/GCLI-159-attribute-write-one-path-read-side for this task to carry F2 and F3 from. THE THREE ITEMS: F1 baseIsRebound is a base-relation reader that read the attribute-write gates; the round-2 finding is that wrapping ALL of it in withoutAttributeGate also turned off GCLI-140's mod.f module-attribute gates, so a base written to an in-repo class was binned external instead of receiver/rebound-base. The fix must bypass ONLY the attribute-write gates inside baseIsRebound, never GCLI-140's module-attribute gates; the m.B = L importer shape is a fixture showing receiver/rebound-base as on dev. Reproduced on dev d58878f, on 034a898 and on the dropped 3b1ace3: m.py 'from ext import B'; y.py 'class L: def g(self)' ; x.py 'import m; class K(m.B): def go(self): self.g()'; w.py 'import m; from y import L; m.B = L' — dev and 034a898 give no edges with receiverNeedsInference 1 and reason rebound-base at x.py:4:9, while 3b1ace3 gives resolvedExternal 1 with reason external-base, an unsound claim that the call leaves the repository. F2 marks every key gated in ANY base's own MRO rather than only the keys of a base the class itself finds gated, so c3merge's first-reached shared entry cannot decide the answer; it only removes, and is a fail-closed removal, not a wrong edge on dev. F3 adds the (a83) item 2 reads: the neighbour attribute and the written module attribute across the write, before and after, both sides agreeing and both dev's. This task gets TWO ordinary review rounds under DEC-161 and is filed before GCLI-156's build. It depends on nothing: it builds on dev fee6946a as it stands.

acceptanceCriteria.text: F1 bypasses only the attribute-write gates inside baseIsRebound and never GCLI-140 module-attribute gates, proved by a fixture for the m.B = L importer shape that asserts dev's receiver bin with reason rebound-base, and by a mutant on the bypass that is observed red

F2 marks a key gated in any base MRO, proved by a fixture running both base orders of E(Outer.F, D) and E(D, Outer.F) with an identical outcome, worded as a fail-closed removal, and by a mutant observed red
F3 the neighbour-attribute and written-module-attribute reads across the write are fixtures, before and after, both sides agreeing and both dev's

The flag-extended subset check over the five pins, every fixture and the corpus shows no created and no flag-changed in-repo edge, with an observed-red control, a floor that fails on a short read and the group count stated; every removed edge is named in the PR
bun run check exits 0 and no DEC-182 path class is touched and no dependency is added

plan: 1. Carry F2 (any-base gated mark) and F3 (the a83 item 2 reads) from 3b1ace3, and narrow F1: baseIsRebound bypasses exactly ONE read, the attr arm head name, so GCLI-140 module-attribute gates and the name arm stay live.

2. Fixtures for every constraint: the round-1 F1 shape, the round-2 m.B = L importer shape, the bare-name variant as a dev-equal control, the R4 bare-base case the narrow bypass first regressed, F2 in both base orders, and F3 reads.
3. One mutant per constraint observed red: F1 head-read bypass off, F1 whole body wrapped again (the round-2 defect), F1 name arm blinded (the R4 regression), F2 any-base mark off.
4. Prove removal-only with the flag-extended subset check from the durable kit at a floor equal to the exact group count, with both controls, then bun run check.
